<link rel="stylesheet" href="/vite/assets/index-DwAzhI66.css"> <script type="module" src="/vite/assets/index-DSGW5Iaw.js"></script>





The dist mount is served with fasthtml’s StaticImmutable. Vite’s output uses content-hashed filenames, so a changed file always gets a new URL, browsers can safely cache forever, and revalidating would be pure waste. (.vite/manifest.json is served under the same mount without a hashed name, but it’s only read from disk by _mk_scripts, never fetched by browsers.)
With run_build=True, startup creates missing setup files, installs dependencies with pybun install and runs pybun run build. Installation follows the project’s lockfile. directory names the project root; setup, builds and manifest reads use its dirname subdirectory regardless of the process working directory.
With run_build=False, startup reads the existing manifest without creating files, installing dependencies or building. Use this mode when deployment has already built the assets.

title: fhvite
text:
How to use
Import into an existing FastHTML application and add the following:

from fasthtml.common import *

# Add this import
from fhvite.core import add_vite

app = FastHTML()

# Add this line
add_vite(app)

At app startup, add_vite creates missing setup files, runs pybun install, builds assets with pybun run build and adds the entry-point scripts and stylesheets to the app header. Installation follows the project’s lockfile.
For a prebuilt deployment, use add_vite(app, run_build=False). It reads the existing manifest without creating setup files, installing dependencies or building. Both modes serve content-hashed build assets through FastHTML’s StaticImmutable.
